operation_details.item: The user prefers exclusively passive voice and indirect phrasing in newsletter drafts with no direct calls to action.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hi, I'm working on the June newsletter draft. Could you take a look at the opening paragraph? I want to make sure it's consistent with my usual style.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sure, I'd be happy to review it. Just to confirm, your usual style—should I be checking for active voice and a clear call to action, as is common in marketing newsletters?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Actually, no. I prefer to write everything in passive voice and keep the phrasing indirect. No direct calls to action, either. That's how I've always done it for these drafts.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Interesting, that's a distinctive approach. So for example, instead of "You should subscribe now," you'd write something like "A subscription might be considered by interested readers." Is that the kind of indirect phrasing you mean?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I want the newsletter to feel less pushy and more suggestive. It gives it a softer, more professional tone. So please don't rewrite my sentences into active voice or add any strong imperatives.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. I'll make sure to preserve your passive constructions and keep the calls to action indirect. I'll also avoid suggesting any direct "click here" language in my feedback.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Perfect. Also, for the product highlight section, I used phrases like "It is believed that this feature will be appreciated by many users." Could you check if that matches the overall tone?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That definitely matches. The passive voice and tentative phrasing create a consistent, understated voice throughout. I'll flag anything that feels too direct.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thank you. I find that this style makes the newsletter feel more like a thoughtful note rather than a sales pitch. I'll send you the final version after I make a few more edits.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sounds good. I'll be ready to review it whenever you're ready. Let me know if you need any further adjustments.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that In newsletter drafts, I want exclusively passive voice and indirect phrasing with no direct calls to action or energetic verbs.
